title.purpose: Section and card headings. Smaller cards use 14px bold.

body.purpose: Default reading and form text at 14px.

label.purpose: Form labels, section labels, badges, column headers.

data.purpose: Patient IDs, referral codes, quantities in tabular Inter.

shadows.name: card-hairline
shadows.purpose: Top-level sheets only; reads as a hairline, not a lift.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Input and keyboard focus. Do not use a colored halo as decoration.

components.name: Filter Pill

narrative.northStar: The Clinic Ledger, with modern SaaS controls
narrative.overview:
AKAY still reads as a well-kept logbook at a health center: white sheets ruled with hairlines on a pale gray desk. Data stays dense and scannable. What changed is the control language. Buttons, tabs, and filter triggers are pills, so daily actions feel like current clinical SaaS (Healthie, Elation, Canvas, Linear) rather than a boxy 2016 EHR. Sheets, tables, and popover panels stay rectangular. Red is still the single mark of attention: the one primary action, the active place, and, in its alert form, danger.

The three-color core is navy ink, brand red, and white. Ink carries text and chrome. White carries readable surfaces. Red is spent once per screen on the thing to do. Ordinary clinical state still uses green, amber, and cyan stamps.

Screens are built for repeated daily work on a desktop or laptop in a facility, sometimes over a weak connection. Loading and error states are first-class. The interface should feel competent and calm on a long shift, never promotional, and never like a diagnosis engine.
keyCharacteristics: Three-color core: navy ink, brand red, white. Status color is extra, not a fourth brand color.
Rectangular sheets and tables with `--radius-card` (12px) on cards and filter popovers; pill-shaped buttons, tabs, dropdowns, and status chips.
One red. Primary actions and active place use it. Alert red is for danger only.
Fixed-size tables: the same row height whether the page has three rows or ten.
Cool-gray neutrals tinted toward blue, never warm.

rules.name: The Three-Color Core Rule
rules.body: Ink, red, and white are the brand. Green, amber, and cyan are stamps, not a second brand. A new module that introduces purple, slate, or rainbow category chips is drift.

rules.name: The One Stamp Rule
rules.body: Red marks the one thing to do or the one thing that is wrong. Brand red is for action and place; Alert Red is for danger. If a screen has red everywhere, none of it is read.

rules.name: The Status-Is-Not-Danger Rule
rules.body: Ordinary state (completed, pending, low stock) uses green, amber, and cyan. Alert Red is never spent on state that is merely noteworthy.

rules.name: The Tokens-First Rule
rules.body: Screens reference role tokens (`--color-text`, `--color-surface`, `--color-brand`, `--color-ink-*`, `--color-neutral-*`) or the ramps in `frontend/src/index.css`. Raw `slate-*` utilities and hardcoded hex such as `#0F172A`, `#F8FAFC`, or `#B91C1C` are migration targets, not part of the system.

rules.name: The Dense-But-Legible Rule
rules.body: Body is 14px, not 16px, because rows and records are the product. Do not go below 10px, and only labels may be that small.

rules.name: The Mono-For-Identity Rule
rules.body: If a value is something a person might read aloud or copy (an ID, a code), it uses tabular figures, not a decorative monospace costume.

rules.name: The Fixed-Frame Rule
rules.body: A table or list card holds its size regardless of row count. Empty and error states fill the same frame instead of collapsing it.

rules.name: The Toolbar-Then-Table Rule
rules.body: Search, filters, and the primary action sit in a compact toolbar above the sheet. Do not insert a second page header, a third filter band, or extra chrome between the toolbar and the rows.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Sheets do not lift on hover. Hover changes a border to Rule Strong or a fill to Ledger Sheet Sunk; it never moves the element or adds a shadow.

rules.name: The Control-Is-A-Pill Rule
rules.body: If the user can press it to change the view or commit an action, it is a pill. If it holds records, it is a rectangle.

dos: Do build surfaces from Ledger Sheet on Ledger Paper with 1px Rule Hairline borders, adding only the card hairline shadow on top-level sheets.
Do use pill buttons, pill tabs, pill dropdowns, and pill status chips. Use rectangular sheets and tables. Filter popovers use `--radius-card` (12px), not a pill and not a square.
Do use Brand 600 (`{colors.register-red}`) for the one primary pill on a screen, Ink for text and chrome, and white for surfaces.
Do reserve Alert Red for danger, urgency, errors, and destructive confirms.
Do use the green, amber, and cyan families for ordinary status.
Do keep table rows at 56px and headers at 44px, and truncate long text with an ellipsis and a title.
Do put IDs and codes in tabular Inter, not a costume mono.
Do reference `--color-*` role tokens or the ink, brand, and neutral ramps instead of raw hex.
Do respect `prefers-reduced-motion`, and keep motion to short fades and state transitions.
Do show locked modules as visible, labeled placeholders.
donts: Don't make buttons, tabs, filter triggers, or filter dropdowns square. That is the retired EHR-minimalism look.
Don't make data tables or filter popover sheets into pills. Card radius on the sheet is required; pill radius on the sheet is not.
Don't lift, translate, or add a shadow to a card on hover.
Don't introduce `slate-*` utilities, rainbow category palettes, or new hardcoded hex values; they are migration targets.
Don't use red for anything that is not an action, an active place, or a danger.
Don't blur real data to indicate a lock; render a placeholder.
Don't make type larger or looser for decoration; density is intentional.
Don't add features that read as clinical suggestions, such as auto-suggested diagnoses or recommended treatments.
